title: SAIT-EMA: A Tridimensional Electromagnetic Articulography Database for Mandarin with Diverse Language Backgrounds
task: Mandarin segment/tone/tone-sandhi/focus materials for native and L2 speakers
annotation_target: EMA trajectories; synchronized audio; syllable initial/final TextGrids; production-error/session screening
annotation_provenance: primary recordings were manually screened against session logs for misalignment/unintentional repetitions; final token set human-verified at recording/item level, but distributed phonetic TextGrids are MFA-generated and the paper explicitly advises manual refinement for high-precision timing
decision_reason: Potentially valuable primary articulatory trajectories, but current evidence does not justify treating MFA segment boundaries as manual. Admit only if the human-verified item-level layer can be isolated without implying manual phone timing.
evidence_summary: 18 speakers; AG501 EMA at 250 Hz and synchronized 48-kHz audio. Paper states misaligned tokens and unintended repetitions were manually screened/removed, while syllable initial/final TextGrids were generated by MFA and can have systematic offsets.

title: Data for studying sonority / Sound level protrusions as physical correlates of sonority
task: production recordings for acoustic sonority study
annotation_target: manually segmented speech used for acoustic analysis
annotation_provenance: Mendeley record states WAV files were manually segmented and analyzed in Praat 4.3.17
decision_reason: Strong primary/manual provenance, but the accessible deposit description advertises raw WAVs rather than the actual segmentation/measurement tables. Locate annotation or derived-measurement files before core row ingestion.
evidence_summary: Primary English and Spanish recordings made in 2005; Mendeley Data version 6 published 2019. Repository explicitly documents manual Praat segmentation and CC BY 4.0, but current public file description needs deeper file enumeration before admission.
